# A centroid cap estimate for simplex tubes in every dimension

Let d>=1 be an integer. Let l(z) be convex and u(z) concave on a compact
real interval, with l<=u. Consider the convex body

    C={(z,x): x_1>=l(z), x_j>=0 (2<=j<=d),
                          x_1+...+x_d<=u(z)}.

Assume its mixed d-volume is positive. At each positive integer fiber put
`r_i=u(i)-l(i)>0`. The positive indices are consecutive, r is a concave
sequence, and the fiber volume is `r_i^d/d!`.

Let g be the TRUE unweighted mixed-volume centroid. Consider a cap through
g of the form

    H={x_1+a z>=b},

so its continuous normal is parallel to the specified simplex facet normal.
Suppose every positive fiber's lower x_1 endpoint satisfies

    l(i)+a i-b<=0.                                     (1)

Thus no fiber lies strictly on the positive side of the cutting plane;
whole-fiber boundary contacts are explicitly allowed. Then

    vol_MI(S intersect H)/vol_MI(S)
                         >gamma_d (d+1)/(d+2),         (2)

where `gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d`. In particular the right side is strictly larger
than `gamma_d/2`. This holds for arbitrary numbers of integer fibers. It does
not require g's base coordinate to be integer, since it estimates one cap
through g rather than asserting that g belongs to S.

Proof. The affine map `(z,x_1,x') -> (z,x_1+a z-b,x')` preserves the mixed
lattice, every fiber's volume, and all ambient halfspaces. It replaces both
endpoint functions by their sums with the same affine function, retaining
convexity and concavity. The tested cap becomes `x_1>=0`, and g's first
continuous coordinate becomes zero. Use U_i for the transformed upper
endpoint and retain r_i for the unchanged width.

The ordinary centroid of the simplex fiber has x_1 coordinate
`U_i-d r_i/(d+1)`. Therefore the true mixed-centroid identity is

    sum_i r_i^d U_i=[d/(d+1)]Q,
    Q=sum_i r_i^(d+1).                                (3)

Let `m=max r_i` and `M=sum r_i^d`. Condition (1) means `U_i<=r_i`.
Consequently the cap's mixed volume, multiplied by d!, is exactly

    F=sum_i (U_i)_+^d.                                (4)

This formula includes U_i<=0, proper cuts, and U_i=r_i at lower-facet
boundary contacts. Zero-volume endpoint fibers contribute nothing and can
be omitted from all sums.

For d=1, (3) immediately gives

    Q/2<=sum_i r_i(U_i)_+<=mF,

hence `F>=gamma_1 Q/m`. For d>1, Hölder's inequality gives

    [d/(d+1)]Q
       <=sum_i r_i^d(U_i)_+
       <=[sum_i r_i^(d^2/(d-1))]^((d-1)/d) F^(1/d).

Since `d^2/(d-1)=d+1+1/(d-1)` and `r_i<=m`,

    sum_i r_i^(d^2/(d-1))<=m^(1/(d-1))Q.

Raising the preceding Hölder inequality to the dth power therefore yields

    F>=gamma_d Q/m.                                   (5)

The proved all-real-power concave-sequence inequality
`candidate 273393b2aa6803aa`, with p=d, gives

    Q>[(d+1)/(d+2)]m M.

Combining this with (5) proves (2); the factors d! cancel exactly. More
precisely, if N is the number of positive fibers, the finite correction is

    F/M>=gamma_d [(d+1)/(d+2)
                          +m^d/((d+2)N M)].           (6)

Every step concerns the actual original mixed-volume sum, and no continuous
projection integral replaces an integer sum.

The restriction to these facet-parallel continuous normals is substantive.
An arbitrary normal on a simplex does not have the single-power cap formula
(4). Nor does (4) remain valid for fibers lying strictly wholly inside the
cap, where U_i>r_i. Those configurations and arbitrary ambient cap directions
are not settled here. Thus this is a bounded higher-dimensional centroid
lemma, not a resolution of general mixed-integer depth or OC.
